ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, ultimate beneficial owners, managers, and authorized signatories against the Luxembourg Financial Intelligence Unit (CRF) lists, the Luxembourg consolidated sanctions list, the EU consolidated financial sanctions list, the UN Security Council consolidated list, and OFAC SDN for USD transactions; enhanced due diligence for PEPs, politically exposed family members, and high-risk third-country nationals; adverse media screening; continuous transaction monitoring and RBE cross-validation under the amended Law of 12 November 2004 and CSSF Circular 18/698.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers - RCS (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés), accessible via lbr.lu and the eJustice portal of the Luxembourg Ministry of Justice
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names may be submitted in French, German, Luxembourgish, or another official EU language; the RCS is administered in French and any non-Latin script must be transliterated into the Latin alphabet; the legal form suffix 'SCSp' or full 'Société en commandite spéciale' must be included; names must not be misleading as to the partnership's object or public order.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: On RCS rejection, the applicant may immediately file a revised name through the LBR portal without additional fee; if the applicant contests the grounds of rejection, a written appeal must be lodged with the Commission of the RCS within 15 days of the refusal, attaching certified search results and justification of distinctiveness; further appeal lies with the Administrative Tribunal (Tribunal administratif) under the amended Law of 16 May 2019; alternatively, the partnership may be incorporated under a permitted name and subsequently apply for a name change by notarial deed and re-registration.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible for the licensed manufacture of sterile examination nitrile gloves. The SCSp must maintain a physical registered office in Luxembourg, and the operational entity conducting ISIC 3250 / NAICS 339113 activities requires an inspected production facility, quality management system, and EU MDR compliance capacity; a virtual office cannot satisfy the commercial substance or regulatory licensing requirements.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (loi modifiée du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), Part IV (Special Limited Partnership provisions introduced by the Law of 12 July 2013); Civil Code articles 1832 et seq.; Grand-Ducal Regulations on the Trade and Companies Register (RCS); Law of 13 January 2019 on the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) administered by Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), 6 boulevard Royal, L-2449 Luxembourg; electronic filing exclusively through the e-RCS portal (myguichet.lu / lbr.lu).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Deed of constitution of the Special Limited Partnership (acte de constitution de la Société en Commandite Spéciale) filed either as a notarial deed or as a private deed (sous seing privé) accompanied by the RCS metadata form; publication in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital and no paid-up capital escrow or bank blockage certificate is required for an SCSp; the partnership agreement must only declare the agreed contributions (cash or in-kind), each partner funds its subscription by transfer to the SCSp bank account within the timeline set in the agreement, and the declaration of contributions is repeated in the RCS filing.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) The annexed partnership agreement constituting the Société en Commandite Spéciale (the 'SCSp') under the amended Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies is approved and adopted. (2) Each founding partner subscribes the Class A limited and Class B general partnership interests in Schedule I; no minimum paid-up capital applies, contributions to be wired to the SCSp account. (3) The registered office is established at [address], Luxembourg, as the administrative seat. (4) [Name] is appointed gérant with full powers of administration and representation. (5) The gérant is authorized to file the deed with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register, file the beneficial-ownership declaration, open bank accounts, and execute all ancillary instruments.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Partner pre-clearance, AML/KYC verification, and drafting of the SCSp partnership agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: External Luxembourg legal counsel (avocat à la cour) applying the AML Law of 12 November 2004 and CSSF circulars; no public filing at this stage
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Collect a certified identification pack for each general partner and limited partner, run sanctions, OFAC, and adverse-media screening, confirm the economic purpose of the manufacturing activity, and draft the partnership agreement covering capital structure, profit-sharing, governance of the general partner, transfer restrictions, termination, and registered office reservation; no minimum capital certificate is required.
required_dossiers: Certified passport or national ID of each natural-person partner
Proof of residence not older than 3 months
Certified corporate KYC pack (articles, certificate of incumbency, ownership chain) for any corporate partner
Registered office lease agreement or address-provider acceptance
Draft partnership agreement and schedule of contributions
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AML pre-clearance is queried, the counsel issues a supplemental information request; refreshed screening reports and updated KYC documents are resubmitted within 3 business days without restarting the schedule.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and, at the parties' election, notarization of the deed of constitution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary (notaire) if a notarial deed is elected; alternatively, execution under private signature before counsel (sous seing privé)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Have all founding partners (or their duly authorised corporate representatives) sign the final counterpart of the deed; where a private deed is used, submit it to the Administration de l'enregistrement for stamp duty registration before deposit; where a notarial deed is used, the notary verifies legal capacity, certifies the signatures, and delivers the authenticated instrument to the RCS without further legalization.
required_dossiers: Final execution counterpart of the partnership agreement
Power-of-attorney and authorization resolutions of corporate partners
Signature legalization or apostille documents for non-resident partners signing abroad
Notary attendance instructions (if notarized)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Drafting or signature errors are cured by re-execution of a rectification deed (acte rectificatif) or a supplementary signing page; missing apostilles are obtained from the competent foreign authority and resubmitted, without restarting the full process.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic filing with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), e-RCS online portal, 6 boulevard Royal, L-2449 Luxembourg
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to e-RCS with a LuxTrust signing certificate; select the SCSp constitution form; upload the executed deed PDF together with the metadata form; enter the registered office, general partner, limited partners, nominal contribution, and gérant details; sign electronically; pay the EUR 44 combined insertion and RESA publication fee by direct debit.
required_dossiers: Executed partnership agreement in PDF
RCS metadata form (identification and capital declaration)
Signed declaration of acceptance of office by the gérant
Registered-office lease or address-provider confirmation
Proof of payment of registration duties
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a régularisation query, the filer submits a corrected deed or supplementary annex within 15 calendar days; the corrected document is registered in the same submission window without an additional RCS filing form or new fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in the Electronic Compendium of Companies and Associations (RESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) acting as RESA publisher, official electronic gazette of companies and associations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon RCS acceptance, the registrar automatically transmits the deed summary to RESA; publication occurs within one business day; the applicant downloads the RESA extract and the RCS certificate of registration as definitive proof of the SCSp legal existence.
required_dossiers: RCS acceptance certificate (automatically generated)
RESA publication extract (downloaded and archived)
Final filed version of the partnership agreement for the archives
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If publication is refused or delayed, counsel files an identical rectified summary within 3 business days; no new fee is charged where the combined RCS/RESA insertion fee was already settled.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Beneficial-ownership registration (Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs - RBE)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (RBE), administered by Luxembourg Business Registers under the Ministry of Justice
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 30 days of RESA publication, file the RBE declaration via the LBR portal; identify every natural person ultimately owning or controlling more than 25% of the SCSp partnership interests or otherwise exercising control; if no qualifying natural person is identified, declare the senior managing officials as the statutory qualifying beneficiary category; attach proof of identity of each declared beneficial owner.
required_dossiers: RBE online questionnaire
Certified identity documents of each declared beneficial owner
Ownership chart evidencing the 25% threshold analysis
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RBE registrar queries the declaration, the SCSp has 15 days to file a corrective return; late filings attract daily penalties of EUR 125 to EUR 250 capped at EUR 250,000 for wilful non-disclosure, and voluntary rectification before a formal notice typically reduces the penalty to a nominal charge.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-incorporation VAT, industrial license, and social security registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (VAT and registration); Ministère de l'Économie - Direction générale des classes moyennes (establishment authorization); Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the SCSp for Luxembourg VAT by obtaining the 14-digit business number (numéro d'identification) once taxable manufacturing activity is contemplated; apply for the Class 1 industrial establishment authorization (autorisation d'établissement) under the amended Law of 2 September 2011; enroll any remunerated gérant with the CCSS within 8 days of taking office; open the SCSp operating bank account to receive the subscribed capital contributions.
required_dossiers: RCS certificate and RESA extract
Final partnership agreement
Autorisation d'établissement application form with criminal record extracts of the gérant
CCSS registration form for the remunerated gérant
Bank account opening resolution and signed signature mandates
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the industrial authorization file is incomplete, the Ministry of the Economy issues a single request for missing items; the applicant may pre-verify the file with the Guichet unique (Maison de l'économie / myguichet.lu) and resubmit within the standard 1-month cure period.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de l'Économie - Direction générale des classes moyennes (Service de l'autorisation d'établissement), jointly with the Administration de l'Environnement for classified establishments; medical device vigilance aspects are coordinated with the Ministère de la Santé - Division de la Pharmacie et des Médicaments (CE marking per EU Regulation 2017/745 on medical devices).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Classe 1 - Autorisation d'établissement pour activité industrielle (Class 1 industrial establishment authorization) for fabrication de gants d'examen stériles en nitrile (manufacture of sterile examination nitrile gloves), together with the environmental operating authorization for the établissement classé under the amended Law of 10 June 1999 relative aux établissements classés.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'Environnement - Luxembourg Environment Agency, Ministry of Environment, Climate and Biodiversity, Département de l'environnement (service évaluations des incidences et établissements classés), 1 avenue du Rock'n'Roll, L-4361 Esch-sur-Alzette
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Classified establishment, Class 2 (autorisation d'exploitation) subject to EIA screening under the Law of 15 May 2018 on environmental impact assessment; the high-speed dipping plant qualifies as an Annex II installation for the production of rubber or plastic products; a simplified environmental impact notice (notice d'impact) is required where annual installed latex-processing capacity exceeds 100 tonnes, otherwise a case-by-case screening decision is issued by the Administration.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: permit limits under the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 20 December 2002 on wastewater discharge (pH 6.5-9; BOD5 25 mg/L; COD 125 mg/L; TSS 35 mg/L; total nitrogen 10 mg/L; total phosphorus 1 mg/L) with mandatory on-site neutralization and latex-coagulation pre-treatment before sewer discharge; air emissions: solvent management plan under Directive 1999/13/EC with an unabated VOC limit of 100 mg C/Nm3 for compounding and curing zones and annual reporting of total solvent consumption; waste: nitrile off-cuts and defective gloves classified as EWC 07 02 13 (plastic waste) and 07 02 99 (unspecified rubber waste), destined only to a licensed incineration facility; landfilling of unprocessed nitrile waste is prohibited.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-safety clearance issued by the Corps grand-ducal d'incendie et de secours (CGI) covering the production hall, nitrile latex storage tanks, and packaging lines, including sprinkler conformity, emergency-exit certification, and hot-work permits for the dipping-line ovens; structural load verification certificate from an approved technical control body (Luxcontrol, SOCOTEC, or TÜV Rheinland) confirming the conveyor dipping-line supports, curing ovens, and foundation loads of the tank farm; workplace safety authorization by the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) covering machine-guard conformity on the dipping and stripping lines, chemical exposure monitoring for nitrile latex and vulcanization accelerants, mandatory personal protective equipment programme, and periodic medical surveillance of authorized operators.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) / Luxembourg Inland Revenue Department; VAT registration is managed by the Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); online portal: MyGuichet.lu (https://guichet.public.lu) and the eCDF platform for tax filings.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Luxembourg SCSp (Société en Commandite Spéciale) with non-resident partners, the partnership itself is not a separate taxable entity for income tax purposes; however, it must obtain a Luxembourg national identification number (matricule) via the Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) and the Luxembourg Business Registers. For VAT purposes, the SCSp must register for VAT with the AEDT by filing the Form 1 (déclaration d'assujettissement) if it performs taxable transactions in Luxembourg without an established business presence, or immediately upon establishment if engaged in taxable activities. The procurement sequence is: (1) file incorporation documents with the RCS via a notary or authorised professional; (2) obtain the 13-digit Luxembourg matricule number; (3) register for direct tax identification if required for withholding obligations (non-resident partners' share of Luxembourg-source income); (4) submit VAT registration application (Formulaire 1) to the AEDT; (5) receive a Luxembourg VAT number (LU + 8 digits + 2 check digits) issued by the AEDT. For foreign entities without permanent establishment, the VAT registration is handled via a fiscal representative or electronic registration on the AEDT portal, accompanied by proof of economic activity, articles of association, and identification of directors/managers.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Under Luxembourg tax law, an SCSp is by default fiscally transparent (pass-through) for corporate income tax, municipal business tax, and net wealth tax purposes, unless it has opted for corporate tax classification (tax-opaque status). The option to be treated as a taxable entity (assujettissement à l'impôt sur les sociétés) must be exercised by the partners in the partnership agreement and notified to the Luxembourg tax administration. Luxembourg applies the EU Anti-Tax Avoidance Directive (ATAD) hybrid mismatch rules, which may disregard the pass-through status of an SCSp if a foreign jurisdiction treats it as opaque and such mismatch results in a deduction without corresponding income inclusion. The check-the-box-equivalent mechanism is not a unilateral US-style election; rather, the SCSp's classification is determined by its legal form and any express election in its constitutive documents, which must be accepted by the ACD. The Luxembourg tax administration also recognises the possibility of filing a request for a tax ruling (tax clearance ruling) to confirm the classification for cross-border investors, subject to the statutory ruling procedure before the Direct Tax Authority.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée, TVA) — Luxembourg VAT system consistent with EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general VAT registration threshold for Luxembourg-established businesses; all taxable persons carrying out taxable transactions are required to register. For occasional taxable supplies by non-established businesses, a de minimis threshold of EUR 10,000 applies to distance sales of goods (Article 65, amended Luxembourg VAT law), beyond which Luxembourg VAT registration is mandatory. For a manufacturing entity selling sterile examination nitrile gloves, VAT registration is mandatory from the first taxable transaction, as no threshold applies to established entities.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg has implemented the EU e-invoicing framework; however, there is currently no mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, no continuous transaction controls (CTC), and no digital stamping requirement for B2B invoices in Luxembourg. E-invoicing in a structured electronic format (e.g., PEPPOL, EDIFACT, XML) is permitted and must comply with the EU Directive 2014/55/EU for public procurement invoices. Since 1 January 2022, Luxembourg mandates the use of the PEPPOL network for B2G e-invoicing by suppliers to Luxembourg public authorities. For private B2B supplies, paper or PDF invoices remain legally valid, but must include the mandatory VAT invoice elements (identification of supplier, recipient, VAT numbers, date of supply, description, quantity, price, VAT rate, and amount). A real-time fiscal clearance system is not currently enacted, but taxpayers should monitor pending EU 'VAT in the Digital Age' (ViDA) proposals, which may introduce mandatory digital reporting and e-invoicing by 2028.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For non-established EU and non-EU sellers, an annual distance-sales threshold of EUR 10,000 applies to intra-Community distance sales and certain cross-border telecommunication, broadcasting, and e-services. However, for in-country manufacturing and domestic supplies, registration is compulsory immediately upon commencement of taxable activity.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg does not operate a fiscal stamping or pre-clearance system. All VAT invoices must be retained in electronic or paper form for a statutory period of 10 years. For the sale of medical devices (sterile nitrile gloves) to EU and non-EU markets, a standard VAT invoice and, where required, an intra-Community sales listing (Listing EC) must be filed with the AEDT on a periodic basis.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods to destinations outside the European Union qualify for the zero rate (0% VAT) under Article 42 of the Luxembourg VAT law, implementing Article 146 of the EU VAT Directive, provided the goods are dispatched or transported to a third-country destination (e.g., the United States, Switzerland, China, etc.) and the supplier retains proper evidence of export. For export of sterile examination nitrile gloves (classified under CN code 4015.12.00), the zero rating applies only if the physical goods leave the EU within the statutory deadline (generally 90 days from supply, or a longer period if contractually agreed and proven). Services closely related to the export of goods (e.g., freight, insurance, warehousing incidental to the export) are also zero-rated under the same conditions. For intra-Community supplies (sales to VAT-registered customers in other EU member states), the zero rate applies under Article 43 of the Luxembourg VAT law, subject to the purchaser's valid VAT identification number, the submission of the recapitulative statement (EC Sales List), and the assurance that the goods are transported from Luxembourg to another EU member state. A VAT-registered buyer in the EU must provide their EU VAT number; the seller must obtain and match the buyer's VAT number in the VIES database and issue an invoice with the notation 'supply intracommunautaire exonéré'.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Déclaration en douane, istrative D.A.U. – Document Administratif Unique)
Bill of Lading (B/L) or Air Waybill (AWB) evidencing physical dispatch from the EU
Inward Remittance Certificate (Bank SWIFT/MT103 or bank credit advice evidencing receipt of consideration in foreign currency)
Proof of delivery (signed delivery note, customs-stamped export certificate or electronic customs export notification from the Luxembourg Customs and Excise Administration)
Certificate of origin (if required by the destination country, for preferential or anti-dumping verification)
For intra-Community supplies: CMR, e-CMR, or other transport documentation and the buyer's EU VAT number confirmed via VIES
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Luxembourg customs and the VAT authorities (AEDT) jointly scrutinise export documentation to prevent VAT evasion and false zero-rating. Where the mandatory documentary evidence is not held by the supplier at the time the supply is declared, or is insufficient, the supply is recharacterised as taxable at the standard rate (16%) or, for certain supplies, the reduced rate (including 3% for medical equipment, if applicable — note that sterilised medical gloves may qualify for the 3% reduced VAT rate on domestic sales, but export zero-rating requires proof of export). The penalties for fraudulent or erroneous export zero-rating include: (i) reassessment of VAT at the applicable rate, plus late interest at the statutory rate (currently 0.8% per month on the amount of tax due); (ii) an administrative fine of up to EUR 25,000 per infringement under the amended Luxembourg VAT law (Article 92); (iii) criminal sanctions in cases of fraud, including imprisonment of between 8 days and 5 years and/or fines of up to EUR 250,000 under the Luxembourg General Tax Law (Abgabenordnung, AO) and the Criminal Code; and (iv) retrospective clawback for up to five years (or 10 years in case of fraud) from the date of the original VAT return, together with interest and penalties. The burden of proof lies on the taxable person to demonstrate the existence of the export and the basis for the zero-rating. Where export is made through intermediaries or under a chain of supplies, additional documentation (e.g., end-user certificates for dual-use medical goods) may be requested.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.export_zero_rating_refund_substantiation: For VAT refunds related to export activities, the exporter claims a credit for input VAT on its periodical VAT return (form 78) filed electronically with the AEDT. For excess credits in an export-heavy model, a refund is processed within 3 to 6 weeks for domestic filing; for foreign entities not established in Luxembourg, refund claims are made under the 13th Directive (non-EU businesses) or the 8th Directive (EU businesses) through the respective member state portal. The refund deadline for non-established EU businesses is 30 September of the following calendar year; for non-EU businesses, the deadline is 31 December of the year following the year of the expense, and the Luxembourg authorities may request additional substantiation, including bank statements, tax certificates of residence, and a power of attorney appointing a fiscal representative.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque Centrale du Luxembourg (BCL); foreign exchange policy and payment system oversight are harmonized within the Eurosystem under the European Central Bank (ECB), with prudential supervision of credit institutions delegated to the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg is a full euro-area member with complete liberalization of capital and current account movements under Articles 63-66 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU). No exchange control regime, no prior licensing, no quantitative restrictions, and no surrender obligations apply to resident or non-resident parties. Dividend, interest, and profit remittances from the SCSp to non-resident limited partners are fully convertible into any currency and freely transferable, subject only to standard AML/KYC, FATCA, and CRS reporting protocols and the absence of any beneficial owner sanctions exposure. The euro is legal tender; multi-currency accounts in USD, GBP, and CHF are standard market practice.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Luxembourg imposes no statutory timeline, no minimum conversion ratio, and no mandatory repatriation or surrender of export proceeds for receivables collected in EUR, USD, or any other currency. Exporters are at liberty to retain foreign currency balances in bank accounts, convert at market rates through licensed credit institutions, or use the proceeds directly to settle trade payables, hedge obligations, or fund operational disbursements.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility is Medium for payment initiation and receipt of funds but Low for any core treasury or trade-finance role. Luxembourg-authorized Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) and Payment Institutions (PIs) under PSD2 can provide segregated client accounts, multicurrency IBANs, and SEPA/SWIFT rails; however, the SCSp's cross-border merchant and trade settlement profile under ISIC 3250 requires documentary letters of credit, pre-export financing, and large-value TT wires that EMIs generally cannot support. Offshore digital EMIs without a Luxembourg or EU passport must be avoided: they are not supervised by the CSSF/BCL and will cause downstream correspondent bank de-risking and drag on account approval with Tier 1 relationship banks.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A physical in-person KYC interview is the prevailing and practically mandatory standard for the SCSp's general partner (GP) director or authorized signatory at the chosen bank's Luxembourg branch or an approved foreign correspondent branch. Because the SCSp is a transparent contractual partnership without legal personality, the account is opened by and held in the GP's name for the account of the SCSp; the bank will require the GP's certified articles, the SCSp partnership agreement, a recent RCS (Trade and Companies Register) excerpt for registered associations, and the notarized/legalized powers of attorney. Remote video onboarding is accepted only for the low-risk corporate profile when combined with strong documentary evidence and prior relationship history; in practice, at least one physical director visit is required before account activation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: SCSp has no legal personality and is not publicly registered in the RCS; banks may flag the absence of a legal-entity structure, a registered office, and independent balance-sheet capacity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized SCSp partnership agreement with a defined euro capital commitment, the GP's RCS certificate and statutes, the CSSF/BCL-compliant beneficial owner declaration (RBE register extract if applicable), organizational chart, and legal opinion from a Luxembourg avocat confirming the SCSp's contractual validity and the GP's binding authority.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial ownership involving foreign limited partners with >25% interest triggers enhanced due diligence under CSSF Regulation 12-02.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Beneficial owner register extract, passport copies, source-of-wealth and source-of-funds documentation (bank statements, asset verifications, tax returns), corporate chain diagram, and negative-news/sanctions screening reports for each partner.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Medical PPE manufacturing and export activity may be treated as trade in regulated goods requiring statutory licenses; unverified supply-chain or end-user information is an underwriting red flag.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: ISO 13485 certificate, CE-marking (EU MDR 2017/745 Class I/Is) documentation, the Luxembourg Ministry of Health import/export license where applicable, factory purchase orders, supply agreements, NDA-protected end-buyer list, and a 12-month cash-flow forecast for the nitrile glove production ramp.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Multi-currency conversion and cross-border payments to non-OECD suppliers trigger correspondent-bank screening for sanctions, trade-based money laundering, and over/under-invoicing.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Auditable commercial invoices, bills of lading, packing lists, inspection certificates, UCP 600-compliant LC drafts, the bank's sanctions and PEP screening confirmation, and an undertaking to use only BCL-approved payment corridors.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial capital injection into the SCSp account from a non-resident partner may be scrutinized where the capital call notices and partnership accounting records are inconsistent.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Capital call notices, GP board resolutions authorizing each transfer, partner bank statements showing the provenance path, notarized loan or contribution agreements, and a Luxembourg CPA (OEC) letter confirming recording in the SCSp's separate accounting.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Non-resident limited partners inject capital via SWIFT MT103 or MT202 for the euro-denominated capital contribution, referencing the SCSp capital call notice and the GP bank mandate. The recommended EU Balance of Payments purpose code is B110 (direct investment in equity capital of a non-financial corporation) or B130 (other capital / partner loan), entered in the remittance field. Funds settle in TARGET2 through the Luxembourg bank's ECB connectivity; the bank will hold the funds on the SCSp's account in the GP's name. The bank requires the capital call certificate, the partnership accounts, and the entry in the SCSp's internal capital accounts; no BCL authorization is required for inward investment.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements are executed via SWIFT MT103 for TT wires to raw-material suppliers (nitrile latex, compounding chemicals, packaging) and via documentary commercial letters of credit (sight or usance, UCP 600) for the export of sterile examination gloves to health-care distributors. Intra-EU supplier payments may be routed via SEPA Credit Transfer. EUR disbursements to other euro-area countries settle through TARGET2; non-euro disbursements are converted at market rate and cleared through the bank's correspondent network. Each outbound payment is matched against the underlying purchase order, invoice, and bill of lading to satisfy the anti-money-laundering and sanctions screening obligations of the correspondent clearing banks.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/USD outright forwards (plain vanilla, tenor up to 24 months) with the Luxembourg account bank under ISDA 2002 with CSA or under the bank's standard treasury line
EUR/USD FX swaps and cross-currency swaps for conversion of USD export proceeds into EUR operational funding
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in exotic emerging-market currencies for input-material sourcing where onshore deliverability is restricted
FX options (European-style, EUR/USD and EUR/GBP) for protective downside coverage on long-term procurement contracts
Commodity-price-linked forward overlays for nitrile latex input costs, where permissible under the SCSp's treasury policy and the bank's derivative eligibility assessment

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial owners (UBO annual re-filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due within one month after the anniversary of the initial RBE registration; due annually thereafter.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines of EUR 125 to EUR 250 per breach under the Law of 13 January 2019. For persistent non-compliance exceeding 12 months, the Public Prosecutor may obtain a court order imposing daily penalty payments; after two consecutive years of default, the RCS may initiate administrative strike-off proceedings against the SCSp.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of annual accounts (conditional – depending on classification)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – RCS (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than seven months after the financial year-end (for a 31 December year-end, by 30 June). SCSp entities exempt from publication under the law of 19 December 2016 may have no filing obligation.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing may trigger an RCS default notice, followed by a court order compelling filing under penalty payment (astreinte). A cumulative two-year failure to file can lead to administrative strike-off (radiation) of the SCSp from the RCS.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A mandatory independent audit applies to undertakings that do not qualify as small under the amended law of 10 August 1915. The small-undertaking thresholds, applied to any two of three consecutive years, are: balance sheet total not exceeding EUR 4.4 million, net turnover not exceeding EUR 8.8 million, and average workforce not exceeding 50 employees. A SCSp exceeding these thresholds, or operating as a CSSF-regulated AIF or public-interest entity, is subject to statutory audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP in accordance with the law of 19 December 2016; IFRS as endorsed by the EU may be used voluntarily where the partnership agreement so provides or for consolidated reporting purposes.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The general partner must identify all natural persons holding more than 25% of partnership capital, voting rights, or control. An initial RBE declaration is filed at registration; changes are reported within one month. A confirmation of the previously filed UBO information is filed annually within one month after the anniversary of the initial RBE registration.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors (general partner and managers)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 2,500 – USD 8,000 (registered office and corporate secretarial services)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,000 – USD 30,000 (if auditing required; exempt SCSp normally no audit)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: An SCSp is fiscally transparent; no Luxembourg corporate income tax (CIT) or municipal business tax is assessed at entity level. Income is taxed directly in the hands of partners. A Luxembourg corporate partner bears the 24.94% aggregate CIT/communal trade tax rate. Preferential mechanisms relevant to the manufacturing scope include the participation exemption (100% exemption on qualifying dividends and capital gains with minimum holding conditions), the 80% IP regime exemption, R&D tax credit/investment credit, notional interest deduction, and the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive 0% WHT on qualifying distributions.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulaire 4 (Déclaration pour l'impôt sur le revenu des collectivités) and partnership allocation schedule; transmitted electronically via the e-CDF portal on myguichet.lu.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (fiscal year normally equals the calendar year unless a different end date is approved by the Luxembourg tax authorities).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 31 May of the year following the fiscal year-end; e-filing automatically extends the deadline to 31 December.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, SCSp legal form, Luxembourg RCS registration number, registered office, central administration address, and matricule number.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State the SCSp's Luxembourg seat; list non-resident partners and each partner's tax residency country and TIN for tax transparency allocation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Profit or loss of the SCSp computed under LIR before profit allocation, comprising revenue from synthetic nitrile glove production and sales, less direct and indirect operating expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute all items applying arm's length principles; any transfer pricing adjustment must be reported also in this box regardless of partner residency.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apportionment of the taxable income to each general and limited partner according to the LPA profit-sharing percentages.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-resident partners, indicate whether the allocated income is attributable to a Luxembourg permanent establishment and identify the applicable DTA provision; income not attributable to a Luxembourg PE is generally not subject to Luxembourg tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Summary of material intercompany transactions (e.g., purchase of latex chemicals, nitrile polymer, equipment; management fees; finance costs) and applied TP methods.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach Local File/Master File if the group revenue threshold is met; specify the tested entity and benchmark for non-resident related parties.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: administrative fine up to €5,000, surcharge up to 10-20% of the tax due, and late-payment interest at 0.8% per month; non-filing after formal notice may result in taxation d'office and, in case of intent, criminal tax fraud liability.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% for SCSp profit distributions (fiscally transparent vehicle; no legal personality); 15% for standard cash dividends paid by a Luxembourg tax-resident corporation; 0% under EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive or applicable DTA for qualifying corporate shareholders.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim treaty relief on Luxembourg source income (if the SCSp is nonetheless characterized as a taxable entity by a treaty partner), the beneficial owner must (i) obtain a Tax Residency Certificate issued by the residence-state authority, (ii) submit the applicable Luxembourg claim/refund form (e.g., Form 770) to the Administration des contributions directes, (iii) evidence beneficial ownership and economic substance (including staff, premises, and real activity) for the SCSp and each claimant partner, and (iv) if tax was withheld at source, claim a refund within the limitation period or request a prior exemption by obtaining an advance tax ruling.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 0% Luxembourg domestic WHT on outbound royalty payments; most DTAs also provide 0% royalty WHT. Interest: 0% domestic WHT on interest paid to non-residents; Luxembourg has no general interest withholding tax; exceptions apply when payments are recharacterized as hidden profit distributions or equity dividends.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 50,000,000 (group consolidated revenue) - exceeds threshold triggers mandatory Luxembourg Local File and Master File for cross-border related-party transactions.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg does not operate a separate ESR code. The economic substance doctrine is enforced through the abuse-of-law doctrine, GAAR (Art. 6 Steueranpassungsgesetz), the EU Anti-Tax Avoidance Directive, and OECD BEPS principles. An SCSp must prove genuine business activity, practical local management, premises, employees, and actual commercial risk to sustain Luxembourg tax residency, claim treaty benefits, and avoid reclassification as an artificial conduit.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately unreported SCSp manufacturing profits, false or suppressed turnover from nitrile glove sales, fabricated deductions, secret bank accounts, or fraudulent reimbursement of personal expenses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment of understated tax plus late interest (0.8% per month); fiscal penalty up to 100% of evaded tax; administrative fines up to €250,000; criminal prosecution if the evasion is committed with intent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: General partner directors and managers may be held jointly and severally liable for civil restitution; criminal courts may impose up to 5 years' imprisonment, travel bans, and director disqualification; veil-piercing is applied where assets are commingled or the SCSp is used as a shield.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to file the annual SCSp partnership declaration or the general partner's CIT return by the statutory deadline; refusing to respond to the tax collector's formal reminders.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Forced assessment (taxation d'office) based on available taxable basis; surcharge of 10% to 20% of assessed tax; late-payment interest; administrative fine up to €5,000; derivative penalties for non-disclosure of foreign relevant assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for administrative fines if they were aware of the non-filing and failed to instruct filing; no imprisonment for simple late filing, but persistent intentional omission can escalate to criminal liability.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Pricing of cross-border related-party transactions (e.g., raw nitrile polymer, chemicals, machinery, management fees) not at arm's length or failure to prepare/maintain Local File and Master File above the EUR 50 million threshold.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Primary transfer pricing adjustment increasing Luxembourg taxable income; denial of interest or royalty deductions; late interest and a penalty of up to 10% on the shortfall; possible corresponding adjustment under the DTA and risk of double taxation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held liable for gross negligence in failing to establish and document arm's length TP policies; personal liability normally requires fault causing tax loss; criminal exposure if the TP policy is a fraudulent sham.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Creation and operation of the SCSp without local premises, employees, bank account, or real commercial risk, used as a passive conduit for treaty shopping / invoice routing of nitrile glove profits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of DTA benefits, EU Directive benefits, and participation exemption; reclassification of income; 20% penalty for abusive arrangements; exit taxation on assets and unpaid capital gains; potential revocation of tax rulings.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and general partners may be jointly liable for crystallized taxes and penalties; in egregious cases, AML and criminal authorities may impose asset freezes, travel restrictions, and imprisonment; the corporate veil will be pierced when the SCSp has no separate economic reality.
